But what he reported and what my assessment was that he was more preoccupied with that rather than that he was engaged in trying to become more socially likeable.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Witness, nothing that you know about would prevent him from being a leader, being accepted by his subordinates as being their leader, is there? There's nothing that you know about that would prevent him from taking that role.

utterances.speaker: ANA NAJMAN
utterances.text: Probably. I wouldn't ...

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Sorry. I am going to have to wait -- "Probably I wouldn't ..." is all I've got. Probably you wouldn't know of anything to prevent that: Is that your answer?

utterances.speaker: ANA NAJMAN
utterances.text: I said that in general when we spoke about that type of personality. I believe that at the beginning I mentioned that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ryneveld. Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just a few questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Will you please tell me: In your practice, is it usual to get the information from case history from the subject and the rest of the work is your own expertise in the assessment of personality?

utterances.speaker: ANA NAJMAN
utterances.text: The information based on case history, whenever possible, that is, if the subject is aware of it, is usually received from him, and that is also of assistance to us, because from the information given by the subject, we see a number of factors of his own personality: what he tries to avoid, what he tries to emphasise, and so on, and evaluate. Also, if it is possible to get hetero-anamnestic information, that is of assistance, but the ones received directly from the subject are crucial.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In other words, the information that is reported by the subject about his case history is not the truth; it is just the raw material, which is then subject to your expert analysis?

utterances.speaker: ANA NAJMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Does the information received by you about his case history deviate significantly or is it in great discord with the information and the findings that you came to through your examination of this subject?

utterances.speaker: ANA NAJMAN
utterances.text: No, it is not at odds, and in working with any subject, this is the procedure that we follow. The information about the case history is evaluated and fitted and clinically analysed within the context of all other material that is available to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me. Is part of your job precisely to distinguish the images that the subject has of himself and what is a more objective view of the subject?

utterances.speaker: ANA NAJMAN
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Taking into account that Mr. Dosen, at the time when he was part of the Keraterm security, was only 25 years of age, he was a young man with very limited life experience, that he was facing situations which were unprecedented in his and in other people's who surrounded him experience, what effects could such a situation have on him, on his personality, the personality of a person such as Damir Dosen was?

utterances.speaker: ANA NAJMAN
utterances.text: I believe that today we have already touched on that, but let me re-emphasise it. This personality structure, with such character traits as hypersensitivity, passivity, a certain kind of dependence and emotional vulnerability and instability, additional stress experiences and unpleasant experiences could only exacerbate his sense of insecurity, inadequacy, depression, and low self-esteem.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: A number of witnesses appeared before this Trial Chamber who said that, for instance, Damir Dosen talked to the detained persons, that he explained to the detained persons that he was not responsible for what was going on there, that he even offered to give them weapons so that they could judge him, that at one point he threw to the ground his belt with a pistol, that he could not take it any more, and things like that. Does all such information comply with the perception that you gained of this subject?

utterances.speaker: ANA NAJMAN
utterances.text: I believe that it does comply. As I said today, the amount of the unpleasant and other things that exert pressure on him which he cannot take, and he finds ways out, either in somatic symptoms or in a sense of helplessness, and that is part of -- that I could put -- everything that you just said I could put under that rubric. He simply cannot find a way out of his passive situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. No more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrovic. Ms. Najman, that concludes your testimony. You are released.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We will adjourn until tomorrow morning at 9.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
